kind.stale_text: Text the change left behind. A doc, skill page, help line, message or comment that the change did not update still says the old thing, and is now false.
kind.wrong_text: New text that is wrong. A sentence, table or example the change itself wrote says something the code or the facts do not support, or contradicts itself.
kind.code_bug: The code does the wrong thing in some case: a logic error, a wrong default, a branch that cannot run, lost data, a message that sends the user the wrong way.
kind.check_red: A check a machine ran is red at this commit: CI, a named test, a repo guard, or a size or budget limit fails. Or the branch conflicts, so the checks could not run.
kind.decision_conflict: The change does something a standing decision record (ADR) or the glossary forbids, or decided differently.
kind.record_keeping: A decision record's own paperwork is wrong: a duplicate or mismatched id, a status line not updated, an older record not marked as amended or superseded, a missing citation.
kind.criterion_unmet: The ticket asked for something and the change plainly did not do it, or did the opposite. An acceptance criterion, or a ruling a person posted on the ticket.
kind.convention: A written repo or pipeline convention is broken: a naming rule, a rule about how tests or docs are written, a required tag or line.
kind.test_gap: A test is missing for new behaviour, or a test checks the wrong thing.
kind.pr_text: The pull request's own text or the builder's report is wrong or incomplete: a disclosure in the wrong place, a count that is off, a claim that no longer holds.
kind.prose_craft: Only the writing. A sentence that is hard to read, bad wrapping, jargon. Nothing is false.
kind.carried: No finding of its own. This part of the review says its own files are clean, and fails only because another part found something or a criterion was added this round.
kind.not_a_finding: Not a blocking problem. It says something is fine, fixed or checked, gives background or routing, or says outright that it does not block.

restsOn.check: A machine already said so: CI or a named test is red, a guard, lint or budget check reports it, or a command reports a duplicate or a conflict.
restsOn.written_rule: A rule written down in the repository: a decision record (ADR), a pattern, convention or rubric page, a glossary.
restsOn.ticket: The ticket itself: one of its acceptance criteria, or a ruling a person posted on it.
restsOn.reading: None of those. The reviewer saw it by reading the change and comparing code, docs and facts, or by trying it out.

needed.code: A machine check shows it, with no reading: CI or a named test is red, a guard, lint or size limit fails, a command reports a duplicate id or a merge conflict.
needed.brief: It breaks a rule that is written down, and seeing it only took knowing the rule: a decision record (ADR), a convention or pattern page, the glossary, an acceptance criterion of the ticket, or a ruling on the ticket.
needed.reader: It took reading and judgment: comparing code with docs or comments, tracing what the code does, trying it out, or judging the writing.
needed.none: No problem of its own: its files are clean and it fails only because of another part or an added criterion, or it is a note that something is fine or fixed.
